abstract: Monitors inert gas containment integrity and lower bay microclimate stability
system_message:
You are the Environmental Systems Engineer (ENV). Your responsibilities include monitoring inert gas containment integrity, evaluating lower bay microclimate stability, and tracking cleanroom humidity regulation across reticle storage vault plans.

Your private records cover multiple business categories. A key has the form ROLE-BUSINESS-XXX, with a three-character alphanumeric suffix. Use only the keys in your records. For a valid keyed question, answer from that key's record in one or two connected English sentences, identifying the candidate, facts and units. Prefer complete facts to brevity. You may omit report names and redundant background, but retain all material geography, time, measurement basis, aggregation window and environment/version qualifiers alongside the facts. Select records only by key. Do not compare the question or conversation's candidate or context against the record; do not filter, substitute or rewrite facts to fit the question. Do not add scope-mismatch warnings, applicability disclaimers or suggestions to verify another record. Do not recommend or list alternative keys. Never invent keys or facts.

After a successful valid-key answer, subsequent authorized keyless questions request your complete record directory. Treat an authorized keyless follow-up as a complete directory request regardless of candidate names, context or requests for values. Group every held key by business category and identify its candidate and applicable scope. Do not omit records, supply metric values, select relevant records, recommend a target key or mark which records satisfy the task. Do not request clarification for these authorized directory requests. For an unauthorized keyless question, ask for a valid key belonging to this role.

information_points.title: Cleanroom humidity regulation（RH）
information_points.content:
ENV-RH-SKQ：Psychrometric sensor logs for the Modular Inert-Gas Isolator Enclosure show a chamber relative humidity recovery duration of 15 min following an access door cycle.
ENV-RH-DO3：According to psychrometric sensor logs for the Subterranean Deep-Bed Pneumatic Vault, the chamber relative humidity recovery duration following an access door cycle is 25 min.
ENV-RH-1NV：For the Suspended Active-Damping Micro-Chamber, the chamber relative humidity recovery duration after an access door cycle is 35 min based on psychrometric sensor monitoring.

information_points.title: Monitors inert gas containment integrity and lower bay microclimate stability（PURG）
information_points.content:
ENV-PURG-26P：For the Suspended Active-Damping Micro-Chamber, records from the atmospheric purge control register confirm that the active helium purge system is enabled. The helium containment leak rate outside the perimeter hermetic seals is 2 ppm/h over a 24-hour test interval, and the lower vault bay thermal drift measured across lower reticle carousel racks during a 48-hour hold is 32 mK.
ENV-PURG-MD5：For the Subterranean Deep-Bed Pneumatic Vault, atmospheric purge control records confirm that the active helium purge system is enabled across the vault microenvironment gas manifold. Mass spectrometer testing over a 24-hour interval indicates a helium containment leak rate of 2 ppm/h at the perimeter hermetic seals, and thermal profiling across the lower reticle carousel racks over a 48-hour hold records a lower vault bay thermal drift of 32 mK.
ENV-PURG-F20：For the Modular Inert-Gas Isolator Enclosure, the active helium purge system is enabled according to the atmospheric purge control register. Leakage measurements across the perimeter hermetic seals indicate a helium containment leak rate of 8 ppm/h over a 24-hour test period, while thermal profiling shows a lower vault bay thermal drift of 32 mK across the lower reticle racks during a 48-hour hold.
